mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 1.5% per annum compresses the risk-free rate component of equity discount models, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in declining FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase above 1.8% per annum signals imminent monetary tightening, which elevates discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 1.8%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in quarterly real GDP (GDPC1) and monthly housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month averages indicate robust aggregate demand, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 and HOUST both > 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 4.0%), the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns due to depressed consumer spending and corporate profit expectations, with the effect being most pronounced over 60-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month average signals weakening supply capacity, reducing corporate output and profit margins, which leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in declining INDPRO periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL reading above 255.0 indicates persistent inflation driven by strong aggregate demand, correlating with rising corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 255.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 12-month averages indicate strong consumer and business spending, driving sustained corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS and HOUST both > 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment expansion regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), the S&P 500 exhibits positive forward returns due to stable labor markets supporting consumer spending and corporate profitability, with the effect being most pronounced over 20-day horizons.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE < 3.5%.
